Description: Fragments of a Hebrew Psalms copy from Qumran Cave 1, arranged stichometrically (verse lines), with the divine name written in palaeo-Hebrew characters. Further fragments of the same manuscript remain unidentified. Preserved-passage ranges for this manuscript are given in English (KJV) numbering; the manuscript itself carries no modern psalm numbers. Note on the Psalm 119 range: the endpoint is given as 119:77-79 following the Study Edition/DJD I; Ulrich's Index lists 119:77-80 — the endpoint is left as 119:77-79 pending resolution.
Significance: An early Hebrew witness to the Psalms, predating the medieval Masoretic manuscripts by about a thousand years. Its chief value is textual: it shows which psalms and which readings were already in circulation in the Second Temple period, and, where its psalm order differs from the Masoretic Psalter, that the order of the Psalter was not yet fully fixed.
